text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Suspension of more than 10 top ports officials in connection with last year's alleged theft of more than 700 cars has been lifted.
- Residents of five villages in Nyambene District in Eastern Kenya flee the area in fear of bandit attacks.
- Production in the Kenya Orchards fruit processing plant in Machakos, east of the capital Nairobi, is suspended following floods at the factory.
- Heavily armed bandits kill nine people and steal at least 2,000 head of cattle in Marsabit district, northeastern Kenya.
- President Daniel arap Moi orders ruling KANU party grassroots elections in opposition-dominated Central Province.
- The plot on which Nairobi's main country bus station "Machakos Airport" stands has been sold to private developers, according to papers filed at the high court.
- The government is losing millions of shillings from the Customs department at the Kenya-Tanzania border.

- President Moi's visit to Bomet district in the Rift Valley ends on a sour note after it turns out that Kipkalya Kones, sacked from Moi's cabinet in January, has gained popularity within his community.
- The Pharmaceutical Society of Kenya is up in arms against bad acts by the Pharmacy and Poisons Board that have given rise to irregular registration of pharmacists.
